newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela recovered $1.1 bln of bank crisis costs.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela recovered $1.1 bln of bank crisis costs.

text.p: Venezuela's Deposits Guarantee Fund (Fogade) said Wednesday it had recovered 529.7 billion bolivars ($1.1 billion) of state money spent trying to bail out failing banks in the 1994-5 financial sector crisis.

The money was recouped from the sale of assets taken as guarantees for aid given to the banks and the re-privatization of banks and other companies that fell into state hands during the crisis, Fogade said in a release.
In nominal bolivar terms, the amount of money recovered was equivalent to 37.8 percent of the total costs of the banking crisis, Fogade said.
But taking into account the steep depreciation of the Venezuelan currency since 1995 the real value of money recovered is equivalent to about 10 percent of the total crisis costs.
About $11 billion in state money was spent during the crisis, which saw about half of the commercial banking sector fall into government hands.
